---
name: iyakki-tile-author
description: Build an IYAKKI tile app, a web page that becomes its own tile in the launcher: files, bridge, headless tests, add to the launcher, publish to a private store
triggers: iyakki app, tile app, tile, launcher, add tile, custom app, calculator app, for iyakki, in the os
---
Use this when the workspace target is "IYAKKI tile app" (see the PROJECT STATE line "Target"). A tile app is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript that runs in its own tile of the launcher on IYAKKI's browser engine. It is NOT a web service: no server, no Dockerfile, no registry, no k3s, no deploy rows, no deploy tools. Never create server.js or a Dockerfile for it.

1. Scaffold once: tile_scaffold {name, dir} (lowercase name). It writes index.html, app.js, style.css, app.json, iyakki-app.json, README.md and tests/app.test.js. Edit those files; do not start a new layout.
2. app.json: id (same as name), name (title shown on the tile), version, icon (one emoji, or a small .png/.svg inside the app), group (default "My apps"), capabilities. Declare only what is used: storage, clipboard, notifications, files, agent (yes/no each), network (a list of exact host names; default none). There is no vault capability and no eval: never ask for either.
3. Write real elements for anything clicked or typed: button, input, select, textarea, a. The engine draws a reader-style layout with CSS (colours, boxes, tables, simple flex); it has no canvas and no mouse events on plain divs. Use a table for a keypad or grid. Keep every file under 500 KB, at most 64 files, no remote scripts, fonts or images unless the host is in capabilities.network.
4. The bridge is window.iyakki: storage.get/set/remove/list (own data, 256 KB, keys of letters digits . _ : -), ui.toast(text), ui.title(text), host.openFile() and host.saveFile(name, text) (promises; the person picks the file), clipboard.read/write, notify.show(title, body), agent.ask(question) (a promise; every question needs the person's yes), app.info(). Calls are rate limited; wrap storage use in try/catch. localStorage is in memory only: keep data with iyakki.storage.
5. Test: write tests in tests/*.js with T.test(name, fn), T.click(sel), T.type(sel, text), T.text(sel), T.eq(a, b), T.ok(c). Run tile_test until it is green. Test the real flow (for a calculator: press 7 + 8 = and expect 15).
6. tile_validate {path}: manifest, icon, size, remote scripts, undeclared capabilities, secrets. Fix every PROBLEM.
7. Try it: tile_install_dev {path} adds it to the launcher as an unsigned dev app (the person approves; administrators only). It reloads when files change. Then tell the person to open My apps.
8. Ship: tile_ship {path}: ONE call that checks, packs, signs with the person's own publisher key (IYAKKI makes and keeps it; never ask the person for keys, accounts or tokens) and publishes to their private store after one approval card. It raises the patch version itself if the store already has this one. If it returns that no private store is deployed, tell the person the one next step it names and stop. (Single steps: tile_pack, store_validate, store_publish.) Installing a signed package from a store shows trust level and permissions first.
9. Board rows for this target: build, test (headless), install to the launcher, verify. Never add a deploy, namespace, image, registry or Job row. A failing test or check gets its own board row with a B- id (never F-): bug_report, fix, verify, attach the passing run.
10. Wrong target? If the person really wants a service on k3s, say so and ask to change the target in the IDE header; do not mix both.
